articles.body: On October 8, 2026, ESMA published an opinion telling MiCA-authorised crypto service providers to stop offering services for non-MiCA-compliant stablecoins to EU clients, and to remediate existing exposure within three months. The outer deadline is January 8, 2027. USDT is the largest affected token. The interesting part for engineers is the shape of the rule. It isn't "remove the asset." It's: Block actions that let EU clients acquire or increase holdings Allow, temporarily, actions that support an orderly exit: sell, exchange, transfer, withdraw Apply per jurisdiction, with dates set by each platform's regulator, inside an outer limit If your asset availability is a single enabled: boolean , you can't express that. Here's a model that can.

articles.title: There's no fall foliage in Phnom Penh, so I built an offline AI that sends me out to flip buckets
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass Pick any October afternoon in Phnom Penh. Around four or five o'clock the sky dumps what feels like a month of r…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass What I Built Pick any October afternoon in Phnom Penh. Around four or five o'clock the sky dumps what feels like a month of rain in twenty minutes, then stops like nothing happened. In a lot of Touch Grass entries this is where you'd go outside and look at leaves turning orange. We don't have that. I'm a student in Phnom Penh and we have two seasons: hot, and hot with a side of dengue. After every one of those downpours, every bucket, flower-pot saucer, old tire and coconut shell on my street turns into a mosquito daycare with free rent. Aedes mosquitoes lay their eggs in exactly that kind of small, still, clean-ish water, and the eggs glue themselves to the container walls.

articles.body: Every paid task has the same hard question: who decides the work is good enough to pay for? I've been earning small amounts from three different answers, so here is a side-by-side. I'm a student and open source contributor (Rust, Node.js), not a Verdikta employee, and one of these systems paid me, so read with that in mind. The three approaches 1. Verdikta: a rubric plus an AI jury, paid from on-chain escrow On Verdikta Bounties the creator writes a rubric with weights, locks the reward in an escrow contract, and two AI models (one from OpenAI, one from Anthropic, 50% weight each) score every submission. If the weighted score passes the threshold, the payout is released. The page for each bounty states that the escrow can't change terms or return the funds before the deadline.

articles.body: Charlie Cox hit New York Comic Con today to join in the Marvel Television panel — jetlagged and just in from Dublin, but ready to talk the return of Daredevil for Season 3 of Born Again. And not just the return of the Horned One, but also his old teammates The Defenders. "I think there needed to be a full circle with that story," Cox told IGN's Jeffrey Vega today after the panel. The Defenders of course originated in the Netflix Marvel era, where each character — Daredevil, Jessica Jones (Krysten Ritter), Luke Cage (Mike Colter), and Iron Fist (Finn Jones) — had their own series before teaming up for the 2017 Defenders season.

articles.title: 9 Legend of Zelda Side Quests Scarier than Any Horror Game
articles.excerpt: Cursed spider families, a ship that sails only at night, and a mummified father in a closet: nine Zelda side quests that belong in a horror story
articles.body: The Legend of Zelda has never been particularly shy about depicting curses, ghosts, and the walking dead (or ReDead). Its optional side quests are where Nintendo tends to let all three run wild. The series has always worked this way — usually giving you a bright, whimsical surface to explore with something rotten and/or horrifying tucked away, should you decide to look under that friendly surface. In the main story, that dread hides inside dungeons and boss fights. In the side quests, the dread has moved into the house next door, where it’s a bit more startling to discover. Curious what nightmares are hiding for Link throughout his various adventures? Check all the closets in the basement, first. Then read on, if you dare.
articles.author: Rebecca Corgan

articles.title: Animals Review
articles.excerpt: The new Netflix thriller Animals is tautly directed by Ben Affleck, who keeps the emphasis on the characters’ flawed humanity. None of the choices available to the protagonists are good ones, and the…
articles.body: Animals is in select theaters and on Netflix on October 9. Ben Affleck is back behind and in front of the camera with Animals, an entertaining new thriller that spices up the kidnap movie formula with a neat twist that asks big moral questions of its protagonists and viewers. Affleck plays Mark Kimball, a tycoon running as an independent candidate to become the next mayor of Los Angeles. (It should be noted that LA is currently in a heated mayoral campaign, so kudos, Netflix, on the timing of your film’s release.) Mark is a middle-aged white male Army veteran with progressive views and a Black wife and mixed-race son, who takes no outside funding and speaks fluent Spanish. It’s a cynical political strategist’s dream candidate come true, something the film acknowledges.
